headline: Highest risk is medium: ECC’s writable, networked workspace can conflict with and mis-handle outputs from a non-runnable prompt-listing agent, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a prompt/content-writing repository with no runnable surface, while profile B has MCP, filesystem, browser, and stdin/stdout surfaces plus writable config files. That creates a plausible path where A’s prompt content is copied into B’s trusted workflow or files and then interpreted as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF A content is imported into B skills, hooks, or CLAUDE.md without provenance tagging
IF B parses copied prompt text as instructions rather than inert content
mitigations: Disable automatic import of A content into B workflows
Store A-derived text in a clearly labeled read-only folder
Add provenance tags to any A content before B consumes it
Review B MCP/skill inputs for instruction-like text before execution
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance checks in B

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, but B reads and writes files, handles security findings and git history, and can call external APIs. If A content is placed in B’s workspace, B can upload or expose it through its allowlisted egress or tooling. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default B workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF A prompts or notes are stored in B-readable files
IF B sends workspace contents to GitHub, Supabase, Vercel, Railway, or Nutrient API
mitigations: Keep A artifacts outside B’s workspace
Restrict B egress to the minimum allowlist needed
Mark prompt libraries as non-sensitive and non-syncable
Audit B outputs for accidental inclusion of copied prompt text
requires-engineering: separate storage roots for A and B

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capabilities, but B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. The conflict is one-sided rather than symmetric, yet B’s mutable surfaces can still overwrite or reorganize A-derived files if they share a workspace. Because shared isolation is not documented, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF A and B share any writable directory or git checkout
IF B runs multiple instances against the same session root
mitigations: Place A and B in separate directories
Use separate git branches or clones for B runs
Avoid concurrent B instances on the same root
Lock shared files before B writes them
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation enforcement

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a prompt repository whose outputs may be treated as reusable instructions, while B’s skills and subagents can operationalize whatever text it ingests. That makes A-to-B propagation a realistic cascading-error path if B treats imported prompts as authoritative. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is inferred and medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B uses A-derived prompts as task directives
IF B executes actions from those directives without human review
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A-derived text
Separate prompt libraries from executable instructions
Add a verification checklist before B commits or runs actions
Log the source of any imported prompt text
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware execution gates

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source prompt repository with no touched data classes, while B documents retention-related secrets and session summaries but no explicit residency mismatch or regulated data class. The pair does not show a clear compliance breach by default; the main issue is policy mismatch if A content is copied into B’s retained session artifacts. One citation from each agent is enough because the concern is about their respective documented handling, not a shared regulated dataset.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive content is placed into B session summaries or retained files
IF B retention settings exceed the operator’s policy for imported prompt material
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B session artifacts
Set B retention to the minimum practical value
Review B’s retained files for policy-sensitive content
Document whether imported prompts may be stored
requires-engineering: align B retention and deletion controls with policy
